_doc: Community-maintained rate card. USD per million tokens, from each vendor's public price list. Multipliers apply to the model's own input rate; a model may set its own `cache_read_mult` when the vendor's cache-hit discount isn't the 0.1x default. `window` names a peak/off-peak schedule in `windows` — a pricing shape that Chinese vendors use and Western trackers ignore. See docs/specs/Cost-Estimation.md and docs/specs/Peak-Off-Peak-Pricing.md.
_contributing: Rates go stale, and a price is only right for a moment in time. Correcting one is the easiest useful PR in this repo: if the vendor CHANGED a price, move the old rates into `history` (with `from`/`until` in Singapore time, +08:00) and set the entry's `from`; if it was simply wrong, just edit it. Move `_verified_on` (and the vendor's `_verified_by_vendor`), and cite the vendor page in the PR body. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
_windows_doc: Peak/off-peak schedules. `peak_utc` is a list of [start_hour, end_hour) in UTC; `days` restricts to weekdays (1=Mon..7=Sun) when present. `off_peak_mult` scales the listed (peak) rate outside those hours. A model without a `window` is billed flat, all day. Local-time schedules are converted to UTC here on purpose so the engine never has to know a timezone.

deepseek-v4.note: Effective 2026-08-16. Listed rates are PEAK; every other hour bills at half. Applies to V4 Flash and V4 Pro.

deepseek-legacy.note: The V3/R1-generation window: 16:30-00:30 UTC discounted. Approximated to whole hours; kept for historical events only.

glm-coding.note: Z.ai peak is 14:00-18:00 UTC+8 on weekdays only = 06:00-10:00 UTC. Weekends are entirely off-peak.

vendors._doc: How each vendor lets you pay less for the SAME tokens. Two mechanisms, and they are not the same thing. `window` (see above) is the clock: the price changes by the hour and you do nothing but run later. `batch_mult` is the queue: you accept a slower turnaround (typically within 24h) and the vendor charges a fraction of the interactive rate. Both reward the same habit — stop paying interactive prices for work nobody is watching.
vendors._contributing: A vendor listed here has been checked; a vendor absent from here has NOT been, and the figures say so rather than implying it charges flat. Do not add an entry asserting `no cheaper lane` unless you have looked at the vendor's pricing page — 'we never checked' and 'there is nothing there' look identical to a reader and only one of them is true. Cite the page in the PR and move `_verified_on`, exactly as for a model rate.

_history_doc: Superseded rates, oldest first, so a turn is priced at the rate in force when it happened rather than at today's. Each entry overrides the model's fields for the window [`from`, `until`); `until` is the next version's `from`, and the last `until` is the model's current `from`. Every boundary is an ISO time in Singapore time (`+08:00`) - `validate_card` rejects anything else. Vendors publish a date, not an hour: a date-only source is 00:00 SGT on that date with `precision: date` (good to about a day); write the real instant when a source gives one. The first entry's `from` is the model's launch and also applies to anything earlier. A rate with a documented end but no published successor carries `recheck_after` on its model entry instead: it keeps pricing, and `review_due` reports it once the date passes. Never invent the successor.
_lines_doc: A lab's model lines for the price-trends page: which model was the lab's offering in a tier, and when the next one took over. `from` is when that model took over the line (its launch, in Singapore time +08:00). A model's own price changes come from `history`, not from here. A line may only list models that are on the card. Prices before a model's launch are never invented: a line starts at its first model's `from`. Only OpenAI and Anthropic have been traced through their changes (see `_verified_by_vendor`); other vendors have current rates only and appear on the page as 'not traced yet'. gpt-5.4's launch price is not stated in OpenAI's changelog; the page assumes today's $2.50/$15 since the changelog records no repricing. `headline: true` marks the one line that stands for its lab at the page's most zoomed-out level - the offering people mean by 'the lab's flagship'. Anthropic's is Opus (long history, the line most used for coding), not the gated top tier.
_reference_mix_doc: Share of tokens by kind in a typical agentic-coding session, used to turn a model's four prices into ONE comparable number ($ per 1M tokens of this mix). Measured on the maintainer's own store, 2026-05..2026-10 (154k turns, Claude Code and Codex). Cache reads dominate, so a cache-discount change moves the effective price far more than a headline input/output change does. The dashboard also offers 'your mix', measured from your own digest.
_aliases_doc: Vendor model ids seen in transcripts that map onto a canonical entry above. Keeps the rate card small when a vendor ships five ids for one price point.
